title: Triage Verdict
description: Verdict JSON emitted by /triage, covering Verify [S1B] (is the trigger real?) and Triage [S2] (identity, two-axis routing per spec §3, §6.4 trap filters, route-or-kill). Kill rules (spec §4): false trigger, tiny spread, mechanical event at Verify; any §6.4 trap fires, peak earnings, fails own balance sheet, ≤15 min/name at Triage. Claude drafts, Vyom skims; the verdict then flows to /lock or to the kill log — either way it is logged (unlogged = doesn't exist). See spec/investment-os-v3.2-master-spec.md §3, §4, §6.4.

identity.description: Identity confirmed first (Constitution rule 4; spec §2.4): company, ticker, exchange, security type, reporting currency, with price date, filing date, and reporting period distinguished explicitly.

ticker.description: Ticker, matching the inbox row that supplied this name.

security_type.description: Security type (e.g. ordinary shares, ADR, preference shares, listed option).

reporting_currency.description: Reporting currency, ISO 4217 code (e.g. AUD, USD).

price_date.description: Date of the price used, ISO 8601. Distinguished explicitly from filing date and reporting period (spec §2.4); tool-verified, never recalled.

filing_date.description: Date the latest relied-upon filing was lodged, ISO 8601 (spec §2.4).

reporting_period.description: Reporting period the financials cover (e.g. FY2026, H1 FY2026, Q2 2026) — distinct from filing date (spec §2.4).

trigger_verified.description: Verify [S1B]: is the trigger real? false forces verdict = kill (kill rules: false trigger, tiny spread, mechanical event — spec §4); when false, the routing axes and trap filters need not be evaluated.

trigger_note.description: How the trigger was verified or why it was discarded — sources with as-of dates (spec §2.4). Time-sensitive facts are tool-verified, never answered from model memory.

axis1.description: Axis 1, the setup router — runs first (spec §3): what carries the value here? earnings_power → proceed to Axis 2; asset_event_option → the matching specialist lens owns method and valuation end-to-end and the name never touches Axis 2.

axis2.description: Axis 2, the economic router — earnings-power names only (spec §3): are today's earnings roughly normal? normal_high_return → Playbook A (durability); depressed → Playbook B (reversion); elevated_peak → default pass, logged with reason 'peak-earnings cheapness'; not_applicable → reserved for axis1 = asset_event_option.

trap_filters.description: The four §6.4 trap filters, run at triage and again pre-entry. Any fired trap kills the name (spec §4 Triage kill rule).

peak_earnings_cheapness.description: §6.4(1) Peak-earnings cheapness → auto-pass: elevated earnings make a stock screen cheapest exactly when forward returns are worst.

melting_ice_cube.description: §6.4(2) Melting ice cube: would volumes recover even if the macro did?

leverage_mirage.description: §6.4(3) Leverage mirage: the business survives, the equity doesn't.

no_unlock.description: §6.4(4) Value with no unlock: no mechanism, no clock (mandatory for B), no alignment.

verdict.description: route = survives kill checks, proceeds to Evidence lock [S3] on the assigned route; kill = logged with kill_reason. Fewer names, or zero, is always acceptable (spec §2.5).

kill_reason.description: Reason a killed name died. false_trigger / tiny_spread / mechanical_event = Verify [S1B] kill rules; peak_earnings_cheapness = §3 default pass and §6.4(1) auto-pass; trap_melting_ice_cube / trap_leverage_mirage / trap_no_unlock = §6.4(2)–(4); fails_own_balance_sheet = Triage [S2] kill rule (spec §4); other = anything else, explained in trigger_note or the trap notes. Kills are logged with their reason — they are data for channel scoring (§5) and calibration (§11).

confidence.description: Stated confidence in this verdict, 0–1. Pre-registered; feeds Brier scoring in Loop 2 (spec §11).

minutes_spent.description: Minutes actually spent on this name. Budget: ≤15 minutes per name (spec §4 Triage row; §13 R&R day 1). Record the true figure even if the budget was exceeded — an overrun is a process fact for calibration, not something to hide.

coverage_class.description: Coverage class declared for the retrieval run (spec §2.1). C0 = user-supplied evidence set; C1 = enumerated universe (full roster/feed, every row processed); C2 = bounded-source harvest — never 'all qualifying companies'; C3 = open-web scout, non-exhaustive sample only, never proof of absence. Dynamic, blocked, paywalled, or truncated sources downgrade the class; more searching never upgrades C2/C3 to C1. All Lane-2 sweeps are C2 unless run against an enumerated feed. Shared enum — identical across all schemas in schemas/; changes only by versioned edit (spec §16).

route.description: Route assigned by the two-axis router (spec §3). A = Playbook A durability (§6.1); B = Playbook B reversion (§6.2); Peak = elevated/peak earnings — default pass, logged with reason 'peak-earnings cheapness'; lens-* = specialist lenses (§6.3): bio/clinical binary, explorer/developer, special situation/cash shell, distressed capital structure, financials/credit, resources producer (B-core method), pre-profit software/tech. Lenses are method vocabularies, not exclusive routes — this field records the primary route (a bank in a credit panic is B with the Financials lens vocabulary). Shared enum — identical across all schemas in schemas/; changes only by versioned edit (spec §16).

fired.description: true = this trap fired; any fired trap kills the name (spec §4 Triage kill rule).

note.description: Brief evidence-grounded justification, required when fired; recommended always (use 'not evaluated — killed at Verify [S1B]' where the check never ran).

trap_check.description: One §6.4 trap check: fired flag plus justification note.
